josh_support: Escalation from Support — AcmeCorp reporting ~10-25% 5xxs on /v1/generate (hosted, us-east-1) starting ~2026-03-15 03:20 UTC. Customer impact: spikes every 5-10m, their traffic is latency-sensitive. They've attached a few request/response snippets.
maria_runtime: Saw the alert. Initial glance: spikes line up with longer prompt lengths and concurrent KV cache evictions. Pushing a quick repro now.
lee_oncall: I'm on it. Can someone paste a sample request ID / headers so we can trace through the gateway logs? I'll open a trace in Tempo.
josh_support: Example request id: req-0a7c9f2e; customer snippet:
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Length: 12456
payload: {"prompt": "<~1500 tokens>...", "max_tokens": 1024}
```
Response: 502 Gateway Error, backend timed out after 45s. Another sample returned 504.
sam_sre: Noted. I'm seeing a correlation in the ingress NLB logs: backend target 10.4.3.21 returned 502s and then circuit opened for ~30s. Patterns show connection resets during KV shard rebalancing window.
maria_runtime: Repro locally with a shaped load (prompt 1400 tokens, concurrency 6) — I can reproduce steady ~12% 500s after about ~3 minutes. Stack trace points to cache lookup + large attention memory blow when sequence length pushes internal memory > capacity on some GPU hosts.
lee_oncall: Immediate mitigation suggestions:
 - roll back the recent attention-kernel micro-optim (deployed 02:50 UTC) on a small canary pool
 - increase gateway backend timeout to 90s for the impacted route temporarily
 - add a fallback model variant (quantized) for requests exceeding 1k tokens
Which one should we try first?
maria_runtime: Rollback kernel micro-optim on canary now. It's quick. Also enabling cache warmup is low risk. I'll start both.
ops-bot: Deploy started: runtime-attn-kernel-rollback -> canary-3 (triggered by maria_runtime). CI link: https://ci.redwood.example/runs/987654
sam_sre: I'm increasing the LB timeout on the route to 90s for us-east-1-lb (ephemeral change). If we still see 5xxs after rollback + timeout then we need fallback routing.
josh_support: Logged customer update: "We have a mitigation in progress, will follow up in 30m." (customer was briefed).
lee_oncall: Quick check: do we have a metric for KV eviction rate? If spikes match eviction windows, that suggests cache being thrash-trigger.
maria_runtime: Eviction rate jumped by 7x right before spike windows. Added a temporary config to increase cache capacity on affected hosts. Patch deployed to canary.
sam_sre: Post rollback + LB timeout + cache size increase — initial telemetry shows error rate drop from 18% -> ~2% in canary. Rolling changes to a subset of production hosts (10%).
lee_oncall: Nice. Action items for the war-room follow-up / postmortem:
 1) maria_runtime: root-cause deep-dive (memory accounting + attention kernel interactions) — due EOD today
 2) sam_sre: runbook update for long-prompt traffic (timeouts, circuit breaker thresholds, fallback routing) — due +48h
 3) lee_oncall: telemetry dashboards to show prom metrics for eviction_rate, seq_len_distribution, backend_open_connections — due +24h
 4) josh_support: customer comms + SLA credit assessment + timeline — initial update in 2h, formal followup after RCA
maria_runtime: Starting RCA now. Preliminary note: certain kernel path uses a transient allocation pattern that races with KV cache compaction under high concurrency; on hosts with low spare GPU memory this leads to OOM-like aborts surfaced as 502s from the runtime.
ops-bot: Rolling update: runtime-canary -> promoted to 10% prod (triggered by sam_sre). Monitor: https://monitoring.redwood.example/d/xyz
josh_support: Customer reports improved success rate in their tests — they see far fewer 5xxs after your rollback. Thanks team :thumbsup:
lee_oncall: We should also capture reproducible test and add to the incident playbook. Maria, can you export a minimal repro harness (curl + prompt) that SRE can run in staging? Put it in #eng-runtime/playbooks.
maria_runtime: Will do. I'll commit a small Python harness + prompt corpus and a checklist to reproduce the eviction pattern.
sam_sre: Next steps for stabilization:
 - permanent fix in runtime kernel (maria) + unit/integration tests (maria)
 - increase default KV cache headroom on hosts serving large-prompt customers (infra change, sam)
 - add auto-fallback to quantized model variant when seq_len > 1024 and backend pressure high (product + runtime)
Assigning owners in this thread.
josh_support: For customer ops: we offered a temporary dedicated pool if they need stricter SLOs while we finish fixes. AcmeCorp asked to wait 48h to confirm stability.
lee_oncall: Postmortem notes we'll want:
 - timeline with deploy->spike->rollback->mitigation
 - root cause: kernel allocation pattern + KV cache compaction under concurrency
 - impact: % of requests failed, affected customers, regions
 - action items (owners + due dates)
maria_runtime: Uploading repro and initial writeup to the incident doc now: https://wiki.redwood.example/incidents/4819991234
ops-bot: Incident ticket updated: INC-2026-481999 created and linked to this thread.
josh_support: Wrapping up: please confirm owners and due dates in this thread so Support/Sales can close the customer loop.
maria_runtime: Owner: maria_runtime — RCA & patch PR by EOD
sam_sre: Owner: sam_sre — infra config + runbook updates by Friday
lee_oncall: Owner: lee_oncall — dashboards + playbook entry by tomorrow
josh_support: Owner: josh_support — customer follow-ups and SLA note by +2h
lee_oncall: Thanks all. If anything regresses ping @oncall immediately. I'll keep monitoring until we close the incident. :white_check_mark:
